verification_qas.question: S1: Is the MV weight construction faithful to WFH09/FWH10 (constraint G^T w = I, Gaussian ideal window, correct covariance integrals)?
verification_qas.answer: YES. mv_weights solves w_i = R^{-1}(Q_i + G lambda_i) with lambda_i = (G^T R^{-1} G)^{-1}(e_i - G^T R^{-1} Q_i), which is the exact constrained minimizer of <(p_i-U_i)^2> with G^T w_i = e_i (verified numerically to 2.2e-16). The ideal window is exp(-k^2 R^2/2); I re-derived the angular integral of Q_{i,n} by hand: n_hat_i * hf2/(2 pi^2) int P e^{-k^2R^2/2}[j0(kr)-2j1(kr)/(kr)]dk matches the code; cov_uu = delta_ij hf2/(6 pi^2) int P e^{-k^2R^2} matches; pair covariance uses the closed-form Gorski Psi_par/Psi_perp with correct A->0 limit sigma_v,1d^2 (card validates 307.96 vs 308.09 closed form, 0.04%).
verification_qas.evidence: htt/obsstat/mv_bulkflow.py:103-138; htt/obsstat/velocity_power.py:75-106; card validation.cell_diagonal_sigma_v_kms=307.96 vs closed_form 308.09; snippet output max|G^T w - I|=2.2e-16

strongest_attack.attack: The MV unbiasedness constraint G^T w = I nulls only uniform (dipole) flows, not a radial monopole; CF4's precomputed Vpec carries a huge deep-end radial systematic (inverse-variance shell means of the actual analysis cells: -612, -1965, -3853, -5765 km/s at r = 220-270, 270-330, 330-400, 400-520 h^-1Mpc — physically impossible as flow, the classic deep-distance-error/Malmquist edge bias), and CF4's anisotropic deep coverage converts it into a fake dipole precisely in the R=150-200 windows that weight the deep tail.
strongest_attack.outcome: Attack CONFIRMED, kill-level. After exactly reproducing the card's |B|(200)=405.22: (1) projecting the pure zero-dipole shellwise-constant field through the ACTUAL MV weights yields a 473.5 km/s response at (l,b)=(333.5,-77.5) — 6.6 deg from the full estimate's apex — robust to weighting choice (unweighted 564.7) and reproduced by the deep shells alone (471.0); data-minus-monopole leaves 84.9 km/s at (274,65). (2) Decomposition-independently: re-deriving the MV weights with monopole-nulling constraints appended (uniform-flow unbiasedness preserved exactly, max|G^T w - I| = 2.2e-16, max|U^T w| = 7e-17) gives |B|(200) = 94.8 +/- 73.7 km/s, chi2_3 = 1.66, p = 0.65 (0.46 sigma), and |B|(150) = 106.2 (p = 0.57), with only modest variance inflation (68 -> 74 km/s), proving the deep dipole is not hopelessly degenerate with the monopole — the estimator simply finds no flow once blinded to the systematic. The headline amplitude, its 'consistency' with Watkins 419+/-36 (whose vector is ~540 km/s away), and the entire 4.4-5.4 sigma range are artifacts of this un-nulled monopole. R=50 results survive (leak 21 vs 173 km/s), consistent with the published-apex agreement being small-R-only.

contrastive.claim: The MV ideal-window estimator with faithful cosmic-variance covariance measures a real CF4 bulk flow |B|(200)=405 km/s (+/-3 binning syst), consistent with the published 419+/-36, in 4.4-5.4 sigma (likely over-estimated per Whitford 2023) tension with LambdaCDM.
contrastive.strongest_alternative: The R=200 headline is dominated by radial-monopole systematic leakage: CF4's precomputed Vpec has a -0.6 to -5.8 thousand km/s coherent radial bias in the deep shells (naive-velocity/Malmquist edge bias and/or ladder-H0 zero-point drift), which the dipole-only constraint cannot null and which anisotropic deep coverage projects into a ~473 km/s fake dipole pointing 6.6 deg from the reported vector; the pipeline's genuine window-200 bulk-flow content is 95 +/- 74 km/s (0.46 sigma, LambdaCDM-consistent), the amplitude match with Watkins is coincidental (vectors 82 deg / ~540 km/s apart), and the card's own out-of-plane apex swing at large R was the visible symptom, misattributed to Psi_par sign structure.
contrastive.adjudication: The alternative wins decisively. Evidence: (a) the leak vector nearly coincides with the reported vector in both direction (6.6 deg) and size (473 vs 405); (b) the effect is robust to the monopole definition (iv-weighted / unweighted / deep-shells-only) and vanishes at R=50 exactly where the pipeline agrees with the published flow; (c) the decomposition-free constrained re-estimate — still exactly unbiased for any uniform flow — returns 0.46 sigma, so a genuine ~400 km/s flow would have survived the nulling (error only 74 km/s) but did not; (d) no physical flow can produce -5765 km/s shell-mean velocities, while deep CF4 distance errors (30-50%) are exactly the known source of such bias; (e) the published Watkins 2023 analysis, using a debiased velocity estimator, reports a stable in-plane apex at all depths — inconsistent with this pipeline's deep vector, consistent with the leak being pipeline-specific. The claim's stated caveats (Whitford covariance realism, P(k) treatment) do not cover this failure mode: it is signal contamination, not variance underestimation, and it removes rather than moderates the tension.

verification_qas.question: S1: Is the FFT GRF normalization in linear_velocity_grid correct (k-space amplitude vs P(k), V/N^3 factors, reality condition)? Recompute single-cell velocity variance on a small grid.
verification_qas.answer: The amplitude convention amp=(N/sqrt(2V))*sqrt(P) is CORRECT in the numpy irfftn convention (<|B_k|^2>=N^2 P/V reproduces <v^2>=(1/V)Sum P; no factor-V or global factor-2 error). BUT the reality condition is NOT enforced on the kz=0 and kz=Nyquist planes of the half-spectrum: independent complex draws there are effectively conjugate-averaged by irfftn, halving their power. Measured per-component variance ratios on n=32/box=2000 over 20 seeds: 0.928/0.927/0.984 (x,y,z) vs the half-power-plane prediction 0.933/0.933/0.993; an exact Hermitian generator (real white noise -> fftn) gives 0.995/0.987/0.995. The deficit is component-anisotropic (v_x,v_y hit hardest because the kz=0 plane carries their dominant low-k modes; v_z modes with kz=0 contribute zero) and is window-weighted large at production scale (naive R=200 ideal-window weighting gives up to 20% in-box deficit, diluted by the exact 37% super-box share to the observed ~7.5%). This bug, not 'grid resolution', is the dominant origin of the reported cov ratio 0.925.
verification_qas.evidence: htt/obsstat/pv_forward_mocks.py:74-92 (rfftfreq z-axis, amp at :83, complex draw at :85, no Hermitianization); snippet outputs: module ratios [0.9278,0.9266,0.9836], exact-generator [0.9951,0.9874,0.9954], prediction [0.9330,0.9330,0.9930]

verification_qas.question: S2: Is super_box_variance the right 1-D variance for k<2pi/L, and is one uniform 3-vector per mock the right physical model?
verification_qas.answer: Formula correct: hf2/(6 pi^2) int_0^kf P dk is exactly the per-Cartesian-component linear velocity variance in modes k<kf (angle-average of k_j^2/k^2 = 1/3). Computed sigma_super=28.2 km/s per component = 37.4% of the R=200 ideal-window variance (5.4% at R=50) — essential and correctly sized. The uniform-vector approximation is reasonable for survey depth (~520 h^-1Mpc) << box (2000), and since the MV constraint G^T w = I recovers a uniform flow exactly, the super-box term contributes exactly sigma_super^2*I to the bulk-flow covariance; gradient corrections from modes just below kf are omitted (second-order for the bulk moment). It is drawn per (box,observer) — independent per mock — matching the module docstring; this makes mocks MORE independent, marginals correct.

findings.title: The load-bearing shape correction pk_corr=(370/308)^2 rests on a refuted premise: 370 is the NONLINEAR sigma_v, not the 'standard linear' value, and EH98 has no ~15% linear sigma_v deficit
findings.detail: The headline 0.40 +/- 0.02 is the raw fit 0.486 +/- 0.022 divided by sqrt(1.4423). The stated justification — 'the EH98 no-wiggle ~15% sigma_v deficit' vs the 'standard linear-theory 1-D velocity dispersion (Planck LambdaCDM)' of 370 km/s — fails direct verification: CAMB 1.6.6 (in the repo venv) at the exact fiducial cosmology and the exact in-repo integral definition gives linear sigma_v_1d = 309.8 km/s, agreeing with the in-repo EH98 value 308.09 to 0.6%; 370 instead matches halofit(mead2020) nonlinear sigma_v = 374.9. Even under a charitable nonlinear reading, the NL/lin ratio of Psi_par/Psi_perp at the separations the fit constrains (10-200 Mpc/h) is 0.95-1.03, not 1.44 — the applied factor is the zero-lag high-k dispersion boost, scale-inconsistent for a large-scale amplitude fit. The 370 provenance is an unverified rev-r195 docstring assertion (contradicted by that script's own 304-vs-308 validation), promoted to a constant in rev-r196. Without the correction the result is 0.486 +/- 0.022: 2.1 sigma from Planck and 4.9 sigma from the published CF4 0.38 at the quoted Fisher precision, so both the headline central value AND the 'consistent with CF4' statement at +/-0.02 are artifacts of the correction. (Spillover note: the same constant in the MV lane only INFLATES a cosmic-variance term, which is conservative there; here it shifts a measured central value, a different and non-conservative role.) The uncertainty of the correction itself is also propagated nowhere, despite being ~10x the quoted error.

findings.title: Headline error +/-0.02 is model-internal Fisher; the 5.3x larger real-data jackknife is dismissed by an undemonstrated assertion, and the card's own consistency tests are adjudicated at +/-0.19, not +/-0.02
findings.detail: The injection MC draws signal from the assumed G and noise from the assumed diagonal N, so 'scatter matches Fisher' (verified: std_A 0.1141 vs data A_err 0.114) certifies the error only under the model. Known-but-unmodelled real-data effects the MC cannot see: (a) Vpec is a Wiener-filter/ramp reconstruction column with attenuated, correlated errors, while N uses raw distance-modulus errors + sigma_star (the card itself calls Vpec 'more model-dependent'); (b) sigma_star for Vpec railed at the lower edge (50.0 = grid[0] of fit_sigma_star's 50..600 grid), signalling the noise model over-covers the WF-smoothed scatter; (c) G's diagonal is the zero-lag point variance applied to inverse-variance-averaged cells (no intra-cell window), overstating per-cell signal variance; (d) no correlated noise (survey zero-points). The delete-one-octant jackknife on the real data is 0.0958 — 5.3x Fisher — and the caveat's explanation ('octant deletion over-perturbs the large-scale field, so it over-estimates') is asserted without any quantitative demonstration (no jackknife-on-mocks exists in the code, which would have been cheap with the reused eigenbasis). Meanwhile consistent_with_cf4/planck use 2*max(jk,0.03) ~ +/-0.19: the claim quotes +/-0.02 next to consistency verdicts that were actually adjudicated at the large error (at +/-0.018 the corrected value is already 1.96 sigma from Planck). A referee would require the jackknife or a demonstrated systematics budget as the abstract error.

Both effects are drawn identically in the injection MC (u = L z + noise from the same G, N), so 'MC unbiased' cannot detect them. verification_qas.question: S2: Could the observed D be dominated by mask leakage of the monopole, and does the mock include the same monopole treatment?
verification_qas.answer: The observed D cannot contain monopole leakage: alpha = sum(w_D)/sum(w_R) per cap makes sum_pix(Dp - alpha*Rp) = 0 exactly, and the dipole numerator uses w = Rp*delta with the same Rp weighting, so the Rp-weighted per-cap monopole of the data delta is identically zero. The MOCK does NOT match this: it uses the fixed data alpha (lam = a*Rp*(1+dmap), delta = (counts - a*Rp)/(a*Rp)) and never re-estimates alpha from the mock counts, so per-cap monopole fluctuations sigma(alpha_hat - 1) ~ 0.007 survive and couple to the dipole through the per-cap footprint dipoles 3|<n>_R| = 2.12 (NGC) / 2.42 (SGC). Measured on a proxy footprint with converged C_ell (60 mocks): fixed-alpha |D| = 0.0191 +/- 0.0082 vs alpha-re-estimated |D| = 0.0135 +/- 0.0060, i.e. the shipped null is ~40% inflated in the mean by this mismatch. The 'IDENTICAL estimator' claim is therefore inaccurate at the delta-normalization step.

contrastive.claim: The window-corrected DESI DR1 BGS dipole D = 9.49e-3 at (l,b) = (172.5, -44.7) is clustering-dominated (far above shot noise) and consistent with LambdaCDM clustering cosmic variance as calibrated by an identical-estimator GRF+Poisson mock ensemble on the real footprint; the kinematic dipole is sub-dominant at BGS depths; no excess/anomaly.

The claim's conclusion stands; its calibration numbers do not.

strongest_attack.attack: Referee report 2 attack: the 95% CL upper limit C_sig < 2.80e-8 (band < 3.28e-6) is quoted as a limit on 'excess low-multipole kappa power', but the flat template is injected at unit response directly into the released masked-reconstruction alm space with no mask/reconstruction transfer — the ACT DR6 release README itself states the maps carry an effective mask M_K^2 and that any harmonic-space analysis 'must be deconvolved (e.g. using the MASTER algorithm)', which 'is not straightforward' — and at fsky=0.234 the ell=2..10 mode coupling is severe. A true sky-level excess C_sig would appear in these alm suppressed by the mask w-factor (order fsky, i.e. roughly 4x), so read as a sky-power constraint the quoted limit is anti-conservative by a factor of a few.
strongest_attack.outcome: The attack lands, but as a P1 scoping/normalization defect, not a P0: (i) the p=0.3525 consistency statement is fully transfer-independent (data and sims pass through the identical masked pipeline; reproduced exactly, 141/400); (ii) the UL is correctly computed and bit-exact reproducible AS a limit on excess power appearing in the released reconstruction alm band — an internally well-defined quantity; (iii) empirical corroboration that the band is not unit-response: the sims' debiased per-ell band power (~6e-8) sits below even the released full-sky N_L alone (8.77e-8), and the release sims/data are demonstrably products of the masked M_K^2-weighted pipeline. The claim text and card nowhere disclose that C_sig is alm-space rather than sky-space power, which a referee would demand fixed (either convolve the injected template with the mask transfer or re-scope the quoted number).

contrastive.claim: ACT DR6 low-multipole (ell=2..10) kappa is consistent with isotropic LambdaCDM end-to-end sims (p=0.35), and a deterministic exact-quadratic injection sets a 95% CL upper limit on excess band power < 3.28e-6 (C_sig < 2.80e-8) above the N0+N1-inclusive sim null — an independent-instrument isotropy constraint, not a detection.
contrastive.strongest_alternative: The analysis has essentially no sky-level sensitivity: the band is reconstruction-noise dominated (N_L ~ 8.8e-8 per mode vs LambdaCDM C_L^kk ~ 1e-8), so 'consistency' is guaranteed rather than informative; the 'mean-field-debiased' step is a numerical no-op on an already-debiased release product; and the quoted C_sig limit overstates sky-level constraining power by an undisclosed mask-transfer factor of order 1/fsky, so the 'real constraint' is weaker than it reads.
contrastive.adjudication: The evidence supports the claim AS SCOPED, with the alternative partially correct on one material point. The p-value and the alm-space UL are exactly reproducible from the raw data (bit-for-bit), the injection algebra is exact, and the card itself pre-empts the noise-domination critique ('reconstruction-noise-dominated; consistency with the isotropic sims is the expected null result', 'noise-floor-limited') — so the consistency claim is honest, not inflated. The alternative wins on the UL's physical interpretation: C_sig is release-alm-space power, not sky kappa power, and neither the card nor the claim discloses this (P1). The mean-field framing point is real but cosmetic (P2): the data IS mean-field-debiased, just upstream by ACT, and the in-house subtraction changes nothing numerically.
